identity_summary: If z=1/N, N = 1/2(a+b) + 1/2 M(a-b), then 1 + delta z + eps z^2 + phi z^3 = 0 is equivalent to 5(a+b)(M^3-M) = (a^2-b^2)(5M^2-1)
notes: Quintic-resolvent reduction. Reduces the cubic-in-z denominator to a cubic in M with parameter (a,b). Note 5M^3-M and 5M^2-1 are related to the modular polynomial for level 5 -- WEAKLY suggestive of modular-form content, but NOT K3.

Closed form for the 4-parameter Ansatz with the extra constraint x{...} = ... -- gives an explicit decomposition of x(x+a)^5+x(x+b)^5 into three 5th powers. The sqrt(5ab) signals this lives over Q(sqrt(5ab)) and may give a K3 over that base, but Ono does not address the 5th-power case at all.

Two-parameter (x,n) family of 5th-power identities. Structurally analogous to Ono's k(T) on the cubic side: a 2-parameter family of solutions to a Waring-type equation. Ono's K3 result is specific to the 3rd-power Pic18 surface; the 5th-power analogue would (if it works) be a different kind of higher-degree algebraic variety, not a K3. Unknown whether any modern arithmetic-geometry paper treats this -- FOLLOW-UP LEAD.

identity_summary: Block 1: theta = 5th root of 2  (= 2^{1/5});  a = 1/(5sqrt(2) - 1),  b = sqrt(5) / [(1 + 5sqrt(4))^{5/2}];  then  a^m b^n theta  =  p_{m,n} + eps_{m,n}  where  |eps_{m,n}| = O( 5^{n/2} / [(5sqrt(4) - 2*5sqrt(4) cos(2*pi*s/5) + 1)^{m/2}  * (5sqrt(16) + 2*5sqrt(4) cos(4*pi*s/5) + 1)^{(2n)/2}] ),  s the most unfavourable of 1,2,3,4
notes: BEST DIOPHANTINE APPROXIMATION to 2^{1/5}. Says: choose multipliers a (= unit in Z[2^{1/5}]) and b (involving sqrt(5) and ratios of (1 + 2^{2/5})^{5/2}); then a^m b^n 2^{1/5} has a rational approximation p_{m,n} whose error is exponentially small in m and n, with the explicit base involving the conjugates of 2^{1/5}. This is Thue-Siegel-Roth-style approximation theory; NOT K3. The product over conjugates is essentially Mahler measure of the minimal polynomial x^5 - 2 = 0.

identity_summary: Block 2: theta = 7th root of 2  (= 2^{1/7});  a = 1/(7sqrt(2) - 1),  b = 7/(7sqrt(8) - 1)*7,  c = (7sqrt(2) + 1)/(7sqrt(4) - 7sqrt(2) + 1);  then  a^l b^m c^n theta  =  p_{l,m,n} + eps_{l,m,n}  where  |eps_{l,m,n}| = O( 7^m * (7sqrt(4) + 2*7sqrt(2) cos(2*pi*s/5) + 1)^{2n} / [ (7sqrt(4) - 2*7sqrt(2) cos(2*pi*s/7) + 1)^{l/2}   * (7sqrt(64) - 2*7sqrt(8) cos(6*pi*s/7) + 1)^{(7m)/2}   * (7sqrt(64) + 2*7sqrt(8) cos(6*pi*s/7) + 1)^{m/2} ] ),  s the most unfavourable of 1,2,3,4,5,6
notes: BEST DIOPHANTINE APPROXIMATION to 2^{1/7} using THREE multipliers a, b, c (vs. two for the 5th-root case). The extra multiplier reflects that 2^{1/7} sits in a degree-7 extension and needs more units to enumerate the best approximations. The conjugate-product structure is the explicit form for the 6 non-trivial Galois conjugates of 2^{1/7}. Again pure approximation theory; NOT K3.

Classic Ramanujan denesting of cube roots: 3sqrt(1/3) + 3sqrt(5/3) is shown to equal three other progressively-more-nested radicals -- the most famous form of Ramanujan's denesting machinery. Citation: Berndt vol IV ch. 16, Andrews-Berndt vol IV nested-radical pages. NOT K3.
Multi-variable denesting / cube-root identity in (a,b). Three explicit radicals on LHS times each other equal a ratio of cube roots on RHS. NOT K3.
